about: Questions an engineer or operator asks of a plant drawing, as data. scripts/question_engine.py runs them over a process model or an extracted twin and writes, for each item a question applies to, the evidence found, the data still needed and where to get it, how the data settles the question, and what a public source says the typical benefit is. A screen, not an audit: it computes no savings for any plant. Rules E1-E26 and C1-C10 follow a research review of public DOE, LBNL, EPA and HSE sources (wording copied from text extracts of those documents); H1-H4 (high-grade heat used for low-grade duty) were added on request and cite the closest source wording, saying so where no number exists. E27-E32, H5, H6, C11 and C12 (refrigeration, ovens, dryers and fryers) were added from a food manufacturer's walkthrough; each quotes S25-S28 with a page, checked word for word against the PDF named in the source's 'checked' note. IAC/ITAC statistics are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch, not re-verified against the download; average dollar figures are deliberately left out. See docs/OPPORTUNITY_SCREEN.md.

fields_help.applies_when: absent_note: a sentence quoted as evidence saying what was looked for and not found. anchor: a selector (or list of selectors, any may match) for the item that triggers the question. with: clauses that must all find a related item. without: clauses of which none may find one. also_show: related items quoted as evidence if present. group_by: unit | item | model. needs_model: item kinds the model must contain, else the question is reported as not checked. min_anchors: fewest triggering items per group.
fields_help.selector: kind (equipment, instrument, valve = control valve, final_element = other operated valve or speed element, hand_valve, relief, controller, interlock, stream, line_item, offpage), type (exact), type_text (regex over type and text), isa (regex over ISA letters), variable, text (regex over tag, name, description and schedule service), text_all (all regexes), not_text, tagged, control_valve, fact_C_min / fact_C_max (a stated temperature fact), schedule_field (the drawing prints this field, filled or blank). not_type_text: optional case-insensitive regex over the explicit type/class only; a match excludes. It does not inspect names, descriptions, IDs or facts; missing explicit type is tested as empty text.
fields_help.relation: same_unit, same_stream, same_unit_same_medium (same unit and same utility: steam, cooling water, air...), other_unit, discharge_side (streams leaving the anchor's unit; on an extracted twin, within max_hops drawn links on the same sheet, direction unknown), near (same unit or stream; on a twin within max_hops links), drives (a controller writing to the anchor), reads (a controller or interlock reading the anchor), anywhere, linked (on a hand-built model: a stream drawn from or to the anchor's unit, an item on such a stream, or the equipment at its other end; on an extracted twin, within max_hops drawn links like near). twin_only / hand_only: true limits a clause to extracted twins / hand-built models. anchor_kind: the clause applies only to anchors of these kinds.
fields_help.data_requests: item, fields (names looked up in the model's facts and the equipment schedule: present = quoted as evidence; printed but blank = the request names that field on that sheet's schedule; a request stays open while any subject lacks a field; field_scope defaults to anchors, requiring each triggering record separately; unit explicitly selects only the finding's owning equipment record, not related context or a join of sources), where (ordered, most direct first: historian (for a role; quantity = flow, temperature, pressure, power, composition or position names only signals that measure it, so a valve position is never offered as a flow; match = a regex the item must match), dcs, nameplate, vendor, maintenance, records, bills, walkdown, or free text), how. show_fields: optional distinct evidence-only fact/schedule names, resolved on the same subjects; present values are unverified candidates and never discharge a collection/review request. Keep required fields and show_fields separate.
fields_help.typical_benefit: wording copied from the source, source keys, arc = DOE IAC/ITAC recommendation code where mapped. Never a figure for a specific plant.
fields_help.evidence_show_fields: Optional literal case-insensitive field names to quote from already-shown anchors and related records only. Values, including blank/null/false/zero, retain their JSON-literal representation, state and exact fact/schedule locator as unverified candidate evidence. These names do not select extra records, change selector facts or complete a request. Native controller/interlock qualifiers remain evidence-only; loop-list CSV records supply no invented fields. When this option is present, the supplied candidate field evidence role is reserved: do not use it as anchor_role or a with/also_show alias. Rules without the option retain their existing roles and rendering.

S12 is not used (no citable sheet survived review). Figures marked 'as reported in LBNL-56183' come from that report's tables, which quote older secondary sources. Where a source quotes dollar figures they are deliberately not copied: they assume one plant's prices and hours.

Collection-contract review (2026-10-30): E1/E2 distinguish generic ratings from matched curves and BEP; E4 retains efficiency and measured-input basis; H4 keeps generic CAPACITY separate from heat duty. Supplied candidate facts cannot close those collection/review tasks. DOE pumping sourcebook S13, printed pp.37-39 and55-61; S14 p.1; DOE Determining Electric Motor Load and Efficiency, https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2014/04/f15/10097517.pdf, printed pp.3-4. This is source-informed development review, not whole-catalog engineering validation.

Collection follow-up (2026-10-30): E11 separates stated process/design temperature from applicable surface/insulation evidence; H1 separates generic capacity, matched steam-throughput rating and actual duration; H2 retains source/reference/state/location/period review beyond named pressure/temperature fields. Source-informed development contract: S1 pp.1-2, S6 pp.1-2 and S8 printed pp.5,9,18-19,54. No additional rule/source-family accuracy or human usefulness result is claimed.

C3 collection review (2026-11-01): review existing named-valve/loop configuration, feedback and performance records before proposing work. Command, local positioner feedback, control-room return, endpoint indication and usable history remain distinct. S13 printed p.26 supports pumping-system variability context; S29-S32 provide scoped vendor examples, not universal capability, quantified benefit or permission for a test/change. Supplied candidate facts do not settle source authority, association or engineering suitability.

questions.question: Is this pump throttled by a control valve when it could run on a variable speed drive?

applies_when.absent_note: no speed control (SC, SIC, SY tag, VFD or VSD) on or next to the pump

also_show.as: other control valve on the discharge

evidence_fields: pump tag and type
control valve tag on the discharge
no speed control (SC/SIC/VFD) shown

data_requests.item: Control valve position (% open) over normal operation

where.what: the valve's controller output
read the positioner stroke indicator at several rates

data_requests.how: Take a month or more of valve output at normal sampling; note the typical and the lowest % open, and the hours at each.

data_requests.item: Flow over the same period (a flow-duration curve)

where.what: production rate records

data_requests.how: Bin the flow into ranges and count the hours in each.

data_requests.item: Pump rated flow and head

where.what: pump curve and rated duty point
pump

data_requests.how: Copy the stated rated flow/head and units. These scalar fields do not establish a matching performance curve or actual operating duty.

data_requests.item: Motor rating and speed

where.what: motor
motor record card

data_requests.how: Copy stated rated output and speed in their original units. Efficiency, identity and drive basis are separate review tasks.

data_requests.item: Static head versus friction head

where.what: elevations and pressures at the suction source and the delivery point
line list or isometrics for pipe lengths and sizes

data_requests.how: Static head = lift plus pressure difference between source and destination; the rest of the pump head at duty is friction plus the valve drop.

data_requests.item: Matched pump curve, rated duty and system operating points

where.what: pump curve and rated duty point
pump

data_requests.how: Retain supplied ratings as unverified candidates. Review the curve against pump identity, installed impeller, speed, fluid, axes/units and revision; distinguish rated duty, BEP and actual operating points. A rating, URI or readability flag does not establish a matching curve or system suitability.

data_requests.item: Motor nameplate, efficiency and drive basis

where.what: motor
motor record card

data_requests.how: Review existing nameplate or motor records for identity, rated shaft output in original units, speed, full-load efficiency and drive/bypass basis. HP/RPM alone do not establish efficiency or measured electrical input; retain missing or ambiguous evidence.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a drive quote when the valve normally runs well throttled for long hours and most of the head is friction rather than static lift (VSDs suit friction-dominated systems best). Close this screening investigation if the valve normally runs near fully open, the head is mostly static, or the pump runs few hours.

typical_benefit.wording: "With rotodynamic pump installations, savings of between 30% and 50% have been achieved in many installations by installing VSDs." Also: "It is estimated that 75% of pump systems are oversized, many by more than 20%."
typical_benefit.arc: 2.4146 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 5,227 recommendations, 3.0 yr average payback, 31.4% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)

questions.limits: On a hand-built model the valve sits on a stream leaving the pump. On an extracted drawing the links have no direction, so the rule takes a control valve within four drawn links that do not pass through other equipment; it may still be on a branch or the suction side, so check the drawing. IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.

questions.question: Is this pump oversized, given a bypass line around it or its valve?
evidence_fields: pump tag
bypass line or valve near the pump

data_requests.item: Measured flow and head at normal operation

where.what: suction and discharge pressure gauges plus a clamp-on ultrasonic flow meter

data_requests.how: Read flow and suction and discharge pressure at steady operation.

data_requests.item: Pump stated rated flow and head

where.what: pump curve

data_requests.how: Retain the stated rating and original units as model evidence; generic CAPACITY/DISCHARGE do not identify BEP.

data_requests.item: How often the bypass is open

where.what: valve position and line temperature
operator logs

data_requests.how: Record bypass position over several shifts.

data_requests.item: Matched pump curve and best-efficiency-point (BEP) duty

where.what: pump curve

data_requests.how: Review the matching curve for installed impeller, speed, fluid and units, then identify its BEP flow/head with source revision and locator. Keep generic CAPACITY/DISCHARGE as rated candidates, not BEP. Retain unknown or unsuitable curve evidence and compare with representative measured operation.

questions.decision_rule: Prioritize the pump if it runs at a flow 30% or more away from BEP or the bypass is used routinely; otherwise close this screening investigation.

typical_benefit.wording: Five indications: "excessive flow noise, highly throttled flow control valves, heavy use of bypass lines, frequent replacements of bearings and seals, and intermittent pump operation." Prioritize pumps "with flow rates of 30% or more from the BEP flow rates, or with system imbalances greater than 20%." No % saving stated.

questions.limits: A drawn bypass may be normally closed; the drawing cannot show how it is used.

questions.question: What do existing records establish about this pump candidate's minimum-flow protection, return-line duty and remaining recirculation question?
evidence_fields: pump candidate
near minimum-flow/RO candidate; actual discharge-return association and flow unverified

data_requests.item: Existing named-pump service, protective minimum-flow and line-association basis

where.what: Existing pump/vendor minimum-flow and service/curve records, actual return-line purpose and routing, protective control function and operating modes; retain exact pump/source/revision/availability and uncertainty.
Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new field test, operating change or retrofit.

data_requests.how: A nearby MIN FLOW, RO or automatic-recirculation label is a candidate, not proof of measured continuous discharge-return flow. Establish the actual pump/service and association first, and retain the vendor minimum-flow protection. Known positive-displacement/vacuum/metering or helper equipment is outside this bounded centrifugal-pump investigation; unknown eligible service stays conditional. Suitable protective operation and existing reviewed records may be acknowledged without a new measurement.

data_requests.item: Existing comparable forward/return flow and duration records

where.what: Existing actual forward and recirculation flow/operating logs with quantities, units, measurement versus valve command, sampling/availability and matching periods/ranges.
Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new field test, operating change or retrofit.

data_requests.how: Preserve source and units; do not substitute valve command for measured flow or divide unconverted/nonmatching records. Review whether sustained bypass is necessary for protection or system function before investigating a remaining energy question. This does not prescribe changing flow, a speed drive, bypass position or protection.

questions.decision_rule: Review the whole pump/system duty and actual operating records with the responsible engineer. Continuous recirculation, an open orifice or missing model data alone is not a diagnosis or instruction to remove/restrict protection. Acknowledge appropriate automatic low-flow operation or suitable existing basis; unresolved minimum-flow, association, quantities or coverage remains a records question. No automatic action or site savings follow.

typical_benefit.wording: "the energy needed to push fluid through bypass lines is wasted." No % stated.

questions.limits: Minimum flow protects the pump; never remove it without the pump vendor's minimum continuous flow. Source review: S13 printed8,15,26,51–52 supports vendor minimum-flow protection and system-dependent bypass analysis, not a universal retrofit. The inherited bypass-energy quotation omits this surrounding protective/system context and is not site savings. Candidate values/labels are not accepted operating evidence.

questions.question: Is this motor oversized for its load?
evidence_fields: equipment tag
motor rating field on the drawing (value or blank)

data_requests.item: Motor rated power

where.what: motor
motor record card

data_requests.how: Copy stated rated shaft output in original units. Full-load efficiency and representative input/load evidence remain separate requests.

data_requests.item: Measured input power or current at normal load

where.what: approved existing motor input-power and representative load/production records

data_requests.how: Retain representative period, coverage, load timing and measurement basis. Prefer documented input kW; three-phase watts derived from voltage/current also need power factor and phase basis. Current alone is unreliable at low load. No new live measurements are instructed; record unavailable evidence.

data_requests.item: Motor nameplate, rated output and full-load efficiency

where.what: motor
motor record card

data_requests.how: Review identity, rated shaft output in original units, full-load efficiency, rated speed/current and source revision. HP alone cannot settle the efficiency needed by the load calculation. Stated output is not measured electrical input; retain unknown efficiency rather than supplying a default.

questions.decision_rule: Load factor = measured input power divided by (rated output divided by rated efficiency). A motor running well below about 40% of full load is worth a resize question; one oversized slightly is fine.

typical_benefit.wording: "At loads below 40% of full load, motor efficiency begins to decline dramatically." "Slightly oversizing a motor (up to 25%) can actually increase efficiency." No % saving stated.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.41xx (category only) (IAC/ITAC browse page: motors: 18,002 recommendations, 2.5 yr average payback, 52.3% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)

questions.limits: Fires only where the drawing carries a motor rating field (filled or blank); a drawing without one gives no trigger. IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.

questions.question: Is fan airflow controlled by a damper or inlet vanes instead of speed?

applies_when.absent_note: no speed control on or next to the fan

evidence_fields: fan tag
damper or inlet-vane actuator
no speed control shown

data_requests.item: Damper position, control mode and operating period

where.what: existing control narratives, drive settings and operating logs

data_requests.how: Use approved existing records. Identify damper/vanes type, fixed or variable speed, bypass/manual modes and representative dates/hours; retain unknown modes and gaps. A drawn device does not establish how it is used.

data_requests.item: Matched fan curves and system operating points

where.what: fan pressure/flow and available power/efficiency curves for the installed configuration
system resistance or required airflow/pressure, operating points and process constraints

data_requests.how: Review the document itself against fan identity/size, speed, gas conditions, axes/units and static/total pressure basis. Retain source revision, locator and suitability gaps; a URI or present/readable flag does not establish a usable matching curve.

data_requests.item: Motor nameplate rating and drive basis

where.what: existing motor nameplate/datasheet and drive/bypass configuration

data_requests.how: Retain original power units, rated speed, asset identity, source and rating basis. Review whether power denotes rated shaft output or electrical input. Do not demand a second unit representation or treat a conversion as measured input.

data_requests.item: Fan electrical-input and load history

where.what: approved existing electrical-input metering and representative fan/process operating records

data_requests.how: Retain period/coverage and coincident airflow, pressure, actual speed/control mode and load timing where available. Distinguish measured electrical input, stated motor output, energy over a period and assumed hours. Record unavailable evidence; this request does not instruct live measurements.

questions.decision_rule: Worth further study when representative records show sustained part-load control and required airflow/pressure can be maintained. A drive quote needs reviewed fan/system curves, operating constraints and electrical-input/load history; the cube-speed relationship alone is not a site estimate.

typical_benefit.wording: Dampers "remain closed so often that they can be found rusted or locked in a restrictive position... the system continually operates against an unnecessary load." Fan "power is related to the cube of fan speed." No % stated.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.4146 (by description)

questions.limits: Damper or drive presence does not establish actual control mode. Fan/system conditions and process requirements need qualified review. Similarity relationships are conditional, not a universal drive recommendation or a quantified benefit for this plant.

questions.question: What do existing records show about this compressor's recycle or blow-off duty?
evidence_fields: compressor
recycle / spill-back / blow-off valve on it
its controller and power measurement if drawn

data_requests.item: Existing control records, machine/service and operating-mode basis

where.what: retained operating/control records with exact machine and valve IDs, record revision and locator
existing approved control documentation, if applicable; controller demand/output is not measured travel or flow

data_requests.how: Start with existing records and check machine class, service and duty. Keep exact machine, valve and record IDs, revision, locator and supplied limitations. Resolve foreign, unknown or shared targets with the record owner; a model association does not verify installed pairing or sibling coverage. Distinguish controller demand/output, actual valve travel and measured flow, including units, quality and reference conditions. Select a representative period from demand and relevant normal, turndown, startup/shutdown and upset coverage, not a fixed month. Acknowledge suitable existing evidence and request only the remaining gaps.

data_requests.item: Applicable machine-protection basis and qualified review

where.what: current site protection/control basis, applicable revision, conditions and responsible reviewer
the appropriate machine-specific operating envelope and protection guidance for the declared service

data_requests.how: Review existing manufacturer/site records with the responsible machinery and controls engineers. Establish applicability to this machine, service, conditions and revision before interpreting a surge line or controller margin. A generic, obsolete or other-machine map cannot establish an excessive margin. Retain unresolved applicability and missing review; do not change settings, operate a valve or induce surge to answer this screen.

data_requests.item: Time-aligned real-power, pressure and flow evidence

where.what: existing energy/operating records with measurement basis, units, quality, time and individual/shared machine coverage

data_requests.how: Check existing records for time-aligned real input power, pressure, flow and operating conditions over the selected duty. Separate measured real power from estimates, nameplate ratings and apparent quantities. Check each record against the exact machine(s) and time covered. Reuse a shared record when its reviewed scope covers the named machines and time; do not infer missing individual coverage from a sibling trace. Keep zero, null and unknown values and limitations explicit. Agree any remaining evidence plan with the responsible owner; no new export, walkdown or test is compulsory when suitable records already exist.

questions.decision_rule: Review the evidence and remaining gaps with the responsible process, controls and machinery engineers. Recycle/blow-off activity can reflect protection and demand; an open valve or a generic margin alone does not establish waste. Turndown/upset-only opening alone neither closes the investigation nor proves a deficiency. Acknowledge suitable working evidence and record the basis for concluding or continuing this screening investigation, its next owner and unresolved questions. No retrofit or quantified saving follows from this screen.

typical_benefit.wording: Blow-off "is a waste of energy and should be used only where necessary to avoid surge." Inlet throttling: "Capacity can typically be reduced from 100 percent capacity to about 70-80 percent with reasonable energy reduction." No % saving stated.

questions.limits: S11 describes compressed-air systems, including centrifugal-air controls; its examples and figures do not automatically apply to process gas, rotary or unknown machines. Establish machine/service applicability first. Supplied machine_class, service and control_records values are unverified claims, including approval/quality fields; showing them does not authenticate their source or establish installed function, protection adequacy or complete coverage. Keep unmatched records, unclear shared coverage and missing reference conditions unresolved. This screen authorizes no operation, test or protection/settings change; any proposed change needs responsible machinery/vendor expertise and the company change-review process.

questions.question: What do existing records establish about this header-letdown candidate's steam service and any backpressure-generation feasibility question?
evidence_fields: header-letdown candidate
actual steam service, two-sided operating requirements and flow-duration association unverified

data_requests.item: Existing station service, steam balance and flow-duration records

where.what: Existing named-station service and current steam balance, actual flow-duration/operating coverage and represented PRV/turbine arrangement; exact source/revision, quantity units, sample period and availability.
Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new field test, operating change or retrofit.

data_requests.how: Establish steam service first: a PRV/PCV or HP/MP/LP/header label alone does not prove steam or two-sided physical topology. Known nonsteam service is not applicable to this steam-turbine question; acknowledge that without a compulsory steam measurement. Missing/unknown data remains qualified. Review existing suitable function before proposing further study.

data_requests.item: Existing actual pressure/thermal, boiler, electrical and feasibility basis

where.what: Existing actual inlet/exhaust pressures and steam condition, process heat requirements, boiler-throughput/capacity implications, annual duty, fuel/electricity/voltage and practical/economic constraints; distinguish design ratings from operating records.
Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new field test, operating change or retrofit.

data_requests.how: The DOE Tip20 source screening figures (3000lb/hr and100psi) describe when to consider further study in its stated context, not automatic install/close thresholds. Do not close an unresolved investigation because data are variable, below an example, unconverted or absent. A backpressure turbine is generally considered in parallel with a PRV and removes energy needed downstream; source prices, graph assumptions/efficiencies and installation percentages are historical examples, not current site savings. Acknowledge an existing suitable function without new measurements or replacement.

questions.decision_rule: Review actual named-station steam service, current balance/flow-duration, process pressure/heat, boiler, electrical and economic constraints before any backpressure-generation feasibility decision. questions.limits: S26 printed p.104 supports dryer process-control examples with several sensor/control approaches; it does not establish the applicability of every oven/roaster/toaster, a humidity threshold or operating safety requirements. Keeping each named subject in source review is authored conservative policy. Supplied labels and literal qualifiers remain unverified; existing company engineering and safety/quality review govern any actual work.

data_requests.how: Retain the original reading type, units and source claim for each named compressor; collect a representative coincident period at known production. A field labelled power or kW remains a supplied candidate and does not prove representative real input power. Amperes, volts, apparent kVA, reactive kvar and a bare cumulative kWh tag are different quantities. Appropriate voltage/current/power-factor and phase evidence, or an energy difference over an explicit matching interval, may support a documented conversion; no conversion or suitability acceptance is automated.

questions.decision_rule: Review the attributed real-input quantity, matching observations, production or refrigeration load and operating conditions before deciding whether additional collection would improve a concrete decision. Existing electrical readings are candidates, including supplied real-kW claims; no tag or quantity field automatically validates the actual basis. A reading nobody reviews establishes no benefit.

typical_benefit.wording: S25 (p. 58): "A basic monitoring system should include ongoing measurement and logging of compressor suction and discharge pressures; a drop in suction pressure typically indicates a refrigerant leak, while a rise in discharge pressure can indicate a blocked condenser (EEBPP 2000a)." "In a review of energy efficiency opportunities for refrigeration systems in wineries, the energy savings associated with the installation of monitoring systems were estimated at 3% (Galitsky et al. 2005b)."

questions.limits: The 3% is one review of winery refrigeration, as reported in S25. Electrical quantity labels, including power or kW, do not validate actual representative input power, circuit identity, conversion or time basis. Keep original claims and uncertainty; no conversion, measurement validity, collection completion or company approval is automated. Fires only where the equipment name, type or service names refrigeration or a supported refrigerant; air, instrument-air, process-recycle compressors and power-plant cooling equipment remain outside this rule.
